Author: dajoey
Name: Gluttony Combo
Punchline: Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.
Description: Gluttony Combo is a lalalazy-branded fork of Wrath Combo. Condenses combos and mutually exclusive abilities onto a single button - and then some. All upstream credit to Team Wrath / PunishXIV.
Changelog:
v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.304 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **While another plugin controls the rotation, a training dummy that is the chosen target is left alone too.** The Manual mode, the manual area-of-effect aim and the Tank Target mode take their target from a selected target - the character's own, or in Tank Target mode the tank's - instead of from the enemy filter that 1.0.4.303 added, so a Striking Dummy that was already selected could still be struck while a lease was held. The same dummy check now covers that path: while another plugin is in control or still holds a lease, the dummy is not attacked even as the chosen target; without a lease the player's own choice stands.
- The external-control check reads the lease table directly on every tick instead of building a list for each read (the rotation consults it several times a tick).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.303 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **Another plugin driving the rotation (AutoDuty and the like) no longer attacks a training dummy, and no longer keeps control after it has stopped.** A training dummy never dies, so a first hit pulled out of combat held the character in combat with it, and the rotation then went on hitting it even after external control had ended. Now, while another plugin controls the rotation or still holds a lease on it, the Striking Dummy is not picked as an enemy at all. External control also does not apply in cities, inns and housing districts or their interiors, so a plugin that walks through one cannot start a fight there. AutoDuty re-asserts the rotation every 5 seconds during a run and goes silent between runs without releasing it, so it now counts as in control for one minute after its last call instead of ten; other plugins keep the ten-minute window. Every job is covered: the checks sit in the shared auto-rotation gate, not in any job's combo.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.302 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **Beastmaster, Crucible: Shield Charge, and the Hawkish Talons finisher that dashes, no longer fire into a boss mechanic that is about to go off or has only just gone off.** The dash asked BossMod Reborn one question: is the landing point inside a danger zone. BossMod Reborn drops a cast's zone and its predicted hit on the tick the cast completes, while the effect is still landing, so the answer turned to "safe" and the dash went on the next tick (11 and 25 milliseconds after it in the replayed logs); for some casts (the Spinner-rook Pieces) it has no zone at all and answered "safe" throughout. The dash now also waits while BossMod Reborn predicts a hit on the character within 3.5 seconds, while the target's cast or a known knockback cast from any caster has 3 seconds or less left, and for 1.5 seconds after any of those, or a danger landing, has cleared. Every automatic dash path is covered: the gap-close, the spend at full charges, the overcap-only spend and the Hawkish Talons finisher. The damage chain is never held and the dash only waits, it is not switched off. Outside the Crucible nothing changes.
- Telemetry: the `dh=` field of an `SG|` line can read `hit-imminent`, `cast-ending`, `knockback` or `settling`, and the decision line's decline list names the same hold (for example `shieldcharge:cast-ending`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.301 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Damage-dealer targeting: the target no longer hops between look-alike enemies about once a second.** In a FATE grind on the Nearest mode, the nearest enemy changes from one press to the next among mobs at almost the same distance, and the one-pick-per-second limit only spaced those hops one second apart. The held enemy is now kept while any press still picks it, and replaced once it has gone 1.5 seconds without being the pick. A dead or untargetable held enemy, the first pick, and boss-mod and Crucible mechanic targets still switch at once, and the one-second limit is unchanged. The enemy an out-of-range press is redirected to follows the same rule.
- Telemetry: the `TS|` line carries the object ids of both enemies (`fid`, `tid`), so a swap between mobs of one species shows as a swap.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.
